2008 [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]] }} '''Tyler Paul Zeller''' (born January 17, 1990) is an American [[college basketball]] player who is currently a senior at the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina]]. He is the nephew of former [[NBA]] player [[Al Eberhard]], brother of [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] basketball player [[Cody Zeller]] and former [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] player [[Luke Zeller]]. ==High school== Born in [[Visalia, California]],{{cite web|url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_tyler00.html |title=Tyler Zeller |publisher=University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Athletic Department |accessdate=March 12, 2011}} Tyler Zeller grew up in [[Washington, Indiana]], attending [[Washington High School (Washington, Indiana)|Washington High School]]. In his four years at Washington High, his team won four sectional titles, as well as state Class 3A championships in his freshman and senior years (2005 and 2008). In his senior year, he averaged 33.1 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 11.0 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, and also shot 69% from the field and 82% from the [[free throw]] line. In his final high school game, the '08 Class 3A final against [[East Allen County Schools|Fort Wayne Harding]], he scored 47 points, which broke a record for scoring by a player in an Indiana boys' state championship game that had stood since 1970. He was not only a basketball superstar, but also played on Washington High's [[tennis]] team for three years, and finished his high school career with a 3.99 [[grade point average]] on a 4.0 scale, good for third in his graduating class. After the 2008 season, he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball award|"Mr. Basketball"]] in Indiana, the state's highest honor for high school players, three years after his older brother Luke was honored with the same award, and was also named a [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]]. During the early stages of the signing period in November 2007, Zeller signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play at North Carolina. When the university announced his signing, Tar Heels head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] said about Zeller, "I think he is the finest running big man in the country and he has a tremendous shooting touch to go with that ability to run the floor."{{cite press release|url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111407aad.html |title=Tar Heels Sign Three To NCAA Letters Of Intent | publisher=University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Athletic Department |date=2007-11-14 |accessdate=2008-11-20}} Zeller notably exhibited that shooting touch at a high school all-star game during the 2008 [[Kentucky Derby Festival]], at which he won the event's [[three-point field goal|three-point]] shooting contest. ==College career== Zeller started the first two games of the [[2008-09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2008-09 season]] in place of the [[2007-08 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|previous season's]] consensus national Player of the Year, [[Tyler Hansbrough]], who was sidelined with a stress reaction in his right shin. In his first game, he scored 18 points in Carolina's season-opening win over [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|Penn]].{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283230153 |title=Thompson powers Hansbrough-less UNC past Kentucky; Zeller hurts wrist |author=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=''ESPN.com'' |date=2008-11-18 |accessdate=2008-11-20}} The Tar Heels' next game, on November 18, was against another equally storied team, [[2008-09 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. The Heels scored a surprisingly easy 77–58 win over the Wildcats, but suffered another injury blow, this time involving Zeller. With 1:26 left in the game, Zeller went for a breakaway dunk off a turnover, but was fouled by Kentucky's Ramon Harris before he could score. Zeller fell to the floor awkwardly, got up, and was taken to the locker room holding his left wrist. [[X-ray]]s showed that Zeller had broken both of the major bones in his lower left arm (the [[radius (bone)|radius]] and [[ulna]]). The day after the injury, he had surgery at [[UNC Health Care|UNC Hospitals]] to repair the broken bones. The surgeon who performed the operation declared it successful, but indicated that the typical recovery time for such an operation is 12 to 16 weeks, making it likely that Zeller will be out for the season.{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=3713121 |title=Broken wrist likely to sideline UNC forward Zeller for season |first=Andy |last=Katz |authorlink=Andy Katz |publisher=''[[ESPN.com]]'' |date=2008-11-19 |accessdate=2008-11-20}} In early January 2009, Zeller's cast was removed. Zeller made his return during his freshman season on February 18, 2009, in the Tar Heels' home game against North Carolina State, playing 8 minutes and scoring 2 points. As a sophomore, Zeller averaged 9.3 points per game on 52.1% shooting and 4.6 rebounds per game in limited action off the bench.{{cite web|url=http://carolinaupdate.com/north-carolina-basketball/roster_player/tyler-zeller |title=Tyler Zeller Career Stats|publisher=CarolinaDaily.com |date= |accessdate=January,06,2011 }} Zeller averaged 15.7 points per game during his junior year. He shot 54.7% and averaged 7.2 rebounds per game. He had a more active role, playing an average of 28.1 minutes per game, significantly more than the 17.4 minutes per game during his sophomore campaign.{{cite web|title=Tyler Zeller|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/41465/tyler-zeller|work=ESPN|accessdate=27 March 2012}} Zeller averaged 16.5 points per game on 55.3% shooting during his senior season. He also played an average of 28.2 minutes per game. Zeller was voted to the All-ACC First Team his senior year and was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]].[http://www.tarheelblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030612aaa.html Zeller Named ACC Player Of The Year – NORTH CAROLINA OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE]. Tarheelblue.cstv.com (2012-03-06). Retrieved on 2012-03-12. Zeller was also named a [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|second team all American]] by the [[Sporting News]] and the [[USBWA]] as a senior. Both accolades make him eligible to have his jersey [[Honored North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball players|honored in the rafters]] of the [[Dean Smith Center|Smith Center]] at the conclusion of his college career. ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;" |+ Season Averages !
